page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.large is an entry-level virtual server within the shared instance family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The hardware configuration consists of 2 shared vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with 2 threads per core on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and provides 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2. The instance includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage and has a baseline network bandwidth rating of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results reflect the shared multi-tenant execution model and constrained resource footprint. In raw compute tests, the instance registered a single-core stress-ng score of 1107.98 and a multi-core score of 2199.5, both ranking in the lowest quartile across tested cloud hardware. Geekbench evaluation shows a single-core score of 957.0 and a multi-core score of 1719.0. Memory throughput achieves 17.08 GB/sec on large-block read operations and 14.55 GB/sec on writes, with PassMark memory scoring 974.98. Static web serving throughput reaches 1.82 GB/sec, while in-memory operations reached 3.0 million Redis SET operations per second.

Because the vCPUs rely on shared hardware allocations without dedicated core isolation or bundled local disks, the server represents an economical compute tier best suited for non-critical services. It functions adequately for lightweight testing environments, internal tools, microservices with low request volumes, and background batch scripts that do not require consistent compute predictability or sustained high memory bandwidth.
